properties.label: Recordings and server data: recordings page [CONTEXT_PATH]/blackbox/  ·  Uploaders view and delete their own recordings; admins every recording. For every recording that reaches it, the server records the recorded tab's Joget log lines and requests (the extension tags them) and a System Info snapshot (the Info tab), plus the parts ticked below. Server data waits on the server until the recording is uploaded, then is kept with it.

properties.name: canUpload
properties.label: Who can upload
properties.description: Empty = any logged-in user. Applies to uploads from the extension and to Import ZIP. Uploaders view and delete their own recordings.

properties.name: canCaptureServerData
properties.label: Who can capture other users' server data
properties.description: Empty = admins only. Who may tick "All server log lines" in the extension's popup (every log line the server writes during the recording, also from other users' requests) and keep a ZIP's server data on import (a ZIP can hold another user's recording). Everyone's own recordings always get, and show, their own server data.

properties.name: maxSizeMb
properties.label: Max file size (MB)
properties.description: Applies to the video and to session.json separately. The recorder stops and saves at 90% of it, so the upload fits. A ZIP import may be up to twice this plus 64 MB.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of MB.

properties.name: maxRecordingMinutes
properties.label: Max recording length (minutes)
properties.description: 5 to 120. Applies to every recording: the recorder shows the time left, warns 2 minutes before, and stops and saves the recording at this length. If the browser doesn't stop it, the server ends the capture 2 minutes later, at this length.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of minutes from 5 to 120.

properties.name: systemLogMaxMb
properties.label: Max size of system logs per node per recording (MB)
properties.description: Each server node keeps up to this much of a recording's log lines (with the other server log lines when ticked in the popup); later lines are dropped and the viewer says the log was cut off.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of MB.

properties.name: serverDataKeepDays
properties.label: Delete server data not uploaded after (days)
properties.description: Server data of a recording never uploaded (log lines, server load, traces, Info, Glowroot data, exported apps) is deleted after this many days.
properties.validation_message: Enter a whole number of days.

properties.name: allowCaptureGauges
properties.label: Allow capturing server load
properties.description: For non-admins; admins may always use it. Samples each node the recording reaches every second: heap, GC time, CPU, busy request threads and database connections, shown as the Server load strip. No Glowroot needed. Each recording gets it only when "Capture server load" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default).

properties.name: allowCaptureTraces
properties.label: Allow capturing Glowroot traces of slow and failed requests
properties.description: For non-admins; admins may always use it. Copies Glowroot's trace of each recorded request Glowroot kept. Needs Glowroot on each node (see "Glowroot address"). Glowroot's own settings decide which requests have a trace (slow or failed); BlackBox doesn't change them. Each recording gets it only when "Capture Glowroot trace files" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default).

properties.name: allowCaptureGlowrootData
properties.label: Allow capturing Glowroot data
properties.description: For non-admins; admins may always use it. Needs Glowroot 0.14 on each node. 30 to 90 seconds after a recording stops, each node it reached cuts the recording out of its Glowroot data, in Glowroot's own format: the traces of the recorded requests, plus the aggregates and gauges of all traffic during the recording. Download it on the replay page and open it in a standalone Glowroot. Each build needs free disk space in Joget's temp folder of about the size of Glowroot's data.h2.db (it is skipped, with the reason, when there is not enough). Each recording gets it only when "Capture Glowroot data" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default).

properties.name: glowrootUrl
properties.label: Glowroot address
properties.description: Used for traces and Glowroot data. Empty = each node's own Glowroot agent (found from its admin.json, usually http://localhost:4000); set = every node uses this address. Read as Glowroot's anonymous user.

properties.label: Support data: the apps the recording used, their data, and the recent changes in the Info tab.

properties.name: recentChangesDays
properties.label: Recent changes period (days)
properties.description: The Info tab's first section lists the app versions and wflow files changed in this period (the app versions narrowed to the apps the recording used and apps sharing their tables). Taken at recording start, with the System Info snapshot. At most 365.

properties.name: allowAppExport
properties.label: Allow exporting the apps used in the recording
properties.description: For non-admins; admins may always use it. When the recording stops (or at upload, when there was no capture or that export failed), the apps found in the recorded tab's URLs (apps with problems first, then the most used; App Center only when it had problems or was the only app) are exported with Joget's own app export (.jwa, without form data, plugins or groups) and kept with the recording. Whose apps: see "Who can export apps they don't administer". Each recording gets it only when "Export the apps used" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default). App definitions can hold plugin settings and environment variables.

properties.name: maxApps
properties.label: Max apps to export
properties.description: Per recording. Apps the user may not have exported don't count. 0 = no limit; empty or not a whole number up to 9999 = 5.

properties.name: canExportOtherApps
properties.label: Who can export apps they don't administer
properties.description: Empty = nobody: only admins and each app's own admins get an app (its definition and data) exported. Users chosen here get only the apps Joget lets them access (one of the app's userviews allows them); other apps are listed as not exported.

properties.name: allowCaptureAppsData
properties.label: Allow capturing apps data
properties.description: For non-admins; admins may always use it. Rows added to each exported .jwa like Joget's own export with data, so importing it imports them: the records the recording opened or saved, rows linked to them, and the newest rows of tables with none; plus the processes the recording touched (read only). Real values and original record ids, except always-masked columns; uploaded files up to 5 MB each, 50 MB per app (larger ones become placeholders). Each recording gets it only when "Capture apps data" is ticked in the extension's popup (unticked by default).

properties.name: allowMaskData
properties.label: Allow masking apps data
properties.description: For non-admins; admins may always use it. Shows "Mask data" in the extension's popup (unticked by default). Ticked there, all apps data is masked: letters and digits get fakes of the same kind, so length and format stay; record ids (primary keys) get new ones, also where other rows point at them, so importing never overwrites rows (the App tab lists old and new ids); process data and user names (user1, user2...) are masked too; uploaded files become placeholders. Kept: option values, yes/no/true/false, numbers up to 5 digits, UUIDs, process ids and values in the app definition; dates keep their year. Without the box, apps data is real.

properties.name: sampleRows
properties.label: Newest rows per table when the recording touched none

properties.name: sensitiveColumns
properties.label: Always-masked column names
properties.description: Comma-separated words. A column whose name has one as a word (ic_no, homeAddress, email-2) is always masked, also when Mask data is not ticked. Empty = the default list.
properties.value: password, ic, nric, passport, email, phone, mobile, tel, address, salary, birth, dob, bank, account, card, iban, ssn
